reason: The sources provide 15 robust, multi-sourced claims that support a captivating 45-second script on the first confirmed isolated stellar-mass black hole.
story: For the first time, astronomers have confirmed a terrifying resident of our galaxy: a completely isolated, invisible 'rogue' stellar-mass black hole wandering alone through interstellar space. Designated OGLE-2011-BLG-0462, this phantom is located roughly 5,000 light-years away and weighs about 7.1 times the mass of our Sun. Since black holes emit absolutely no light, it was impossible to see directly. Instead, scientists detected it when its intense gravity warped and brightened the light of a background star 20,000 light-years away—a phenomenon called gravitational microlensing. Using the Hubble Space Telescope and ground-based surveys, astronomers painstakingly monitored the star over six years. By proving the lensing object emitted no light of its own, they confirmed it was a black hole. Even more chilling, this cosmic ghost is hurtling through our galactic neighborhood at a blistering 45 to 51 kilometers per second.
angle: Astronomers have confirmed the first-ever completely isolated, invisible 'rogue' stellar-mass black hole drifting completely alone through our galaxy, and it is traveling at up to 51 kilometers per second.

claims.claim: OGLE-2011-BLG-0462 is an isolated stellar-mass black hole drifting in interstellar space.
It is the first confirmed isolated stellar-mass black hole ever detected.
It is not gravitationally bound to any other astronomical object.
The black hole was detected using gravitational microlensing.
The microlensing event occurred when the black hole's gravity bent and magnified the light of a background star.
The background star whose light was warped is located approximately 20,000 light-years away from Earth.
The black hole itself is located about 5,000 light-years away from Earth.
It has a mass of approximately 7.1 to 7.15 times that of our Sun.
The Hubble Space Telescope was used to measure the deflections in the background star's position.
The ground-based Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment (OGLE) survey originally detected the event.
The initial event began in 2011 with a sudden spike in the brightness of the background star.
Confirming the black hole required an observational campaign lasting about six years.
Astronomers confirmed it was a black hole by verifying that the lensing object itself emitted no light.
The black hole is traveling through space at an estimated speed of 45 to 51 kilometers per second.
Its traveling velocity is significantly faster than the neighboring stars in that region of the galaxy.

disputed: The black hole's exact distance varies between S1 (5,610 light-years) and S2, S3, S4 (approximately 5,000 light-years). The script should refer to it as about 5,000 light-years away using the latest research.

The speed of the black hole is reported as 45 km/s in S2 and S3, but calculated at 51.1 km/s in S4, with S1 noting an upper limit of 100 km/s. The script should use a range of 45 to 51 kilometers per second.
The estimated age of the black hole and when it was kicked is reported as 100 million years ago only in S3. Since it is unverified by other sites, it should be omitted or labeled as a rough estimate.
